nodes.label: Participant
nodes.summary: Joins a call from a browser or a native app and sends and receives audio, video and screen share.

nodes.label: Media client
nodes.summary: Browser WebRTC, or a native C++ engine on the WebRTC library that can skip SDP and ICE, use Salsa20, and send nothing during silence (Discord).

nodes.label: Gateway
nodes.summary: Long-lived WebSocket per online client carrying events and voice state updates (Elixir at Discord).

nodes.label: Call placement
nodes.summary: Discord Guilds: assigns the least utilized voice server in the region to the guild, pushes voice state to it, and reassigns on failure, DDoS or region change.

nodes.label: Service discovery
nodes.summary: Voice servers report health and load here; a server that fails its ping is removed.

nodes.label: Media server
nodes.summary: One of hundreds of regional voice servers; each pairs a signaling component with an SFU.

nodes.label: Server signaling
nodes.summary: Controls the SFU: stream ids, encryption keys, speaking indication; restarts a crashed SFU and rebuilds its state without clients.

nodes.label: Selective forwarding unit
nodes.summary: Forwards RTP packets without decoding the payload, choosing which sources each endpoint receives; drops muted users' packets, bridges browser and native transports, handles RTCP.

nodes.label: Speaker selection (Last N)
nodes.summary: Orders endpoints by audio activity and forwards video from the last N dominant speakers: 45% less CPU and 63% less bandwidth for 10 of 30 participants (Jitsi).

nodes.label: TURN relay
nodes.summary: Relays media for hosts that cannot communicate directly behind NATs; used by ICE as the last-resort path.

steps.caption: The client asks to join a voice channel over its existing gateway WebSocket.
Its voice state is updated in the placement service.
If the call has no server yet, the least utilized voice server in the region is picked.
All voice states are pushed to that server so it can set up forwarding.
The client opens a voice WebSocket to the server and exchanges keys and stream ids.
Media flows over UDP to and from the SFU.
Each sender sends its streams once to the SFU.
Audio levels rank the speakers; only the last N speakers' video is selected.
Each receiver gets those streams, without the SFU decoding or re-encoding them.

flows.name: A client behind a strict NAT

steps.caption: Direct UDP to the SFU fails, so ICE selects the relayed candidate.
The TURN server relays the media, at the cost of an extra hop.
Signaling sees the SFU is gone and restarts it right away.
It rebuilds the SFU's state itself; clients see only a few dropped packets.

flows.name: The media server dies or is attacked (failure)

steps.caption: The server fails its ping (or is pulled for a DDoS) and leaves service discovery.
Clients notice the dropped voice WebSocket and report it over the gateway.
Placement confirms and picks a new server in the region.
It pushes the voice states to the new server.
Clients reconnect to the new server and media resumes.
